title: Annotation
description: Ground-truth story boundaries for one transcript. JSONL: one object per line, UTF-8. Joined to a transcript by `record_id`. Note that an annotation carries no text -- only offsets -- which is what makes an annotation set distributable when the underlying transcripts are licensed.

record_id.description: Must match a transcript's `record_id`. An annotation with no matching transcript is a hard error.

breaks.description: Word offsets at which a NEW story begins, i.e. the index in `body.split()` of the first word of the new story. Ascending, unique, and strictly interior: every offset must satisfy 0 < b < word_count. Offset 0 is not a boundary -- every document starts a story -- and neither is word_count. An empty array is meaningful and common: 306 of the 998 training transcripts contain no boundary at all.

word_count.description: Must equal the matching transcript's `word_count`. This is the guard that catches an annotation made against a different revision of the text -- the single most damaging silent error in this pipeline.

category.description: `A` = the transcript contains at least one boundary. `C` = clean, no boundary. Redundant with `breaks` by construction (A iff breaks is non-empty) and retained because the training set routes the two categories differently. Training corpus: 692 A, 306 C.

outlet.description: Copied from the transcript for convenience; the transcript is authoritative.

show.description: Copied from the transcript for convenience; the transcript is authoritative.

date.description: Copied from the transcript for convenience; the transcript is authoritative.

agent_notes.description: Free-text rationale from the annotator. Never read by training or inference; kept for adjudication and for auditing granularity disagreements.
